one_line: An interactive mystery manuscript whose discoveries unlock new WebMCP capabilities for the agent.
what_it_does: Once Upon lets a human and agent explore an authored mystery through natural-language actions; story discoveries reveal structured tools, and using those tools updates the canonical narrative state.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is presented as a central narrative mechanic rather than a simple UI wrapper: the story controls which structured actions exist, the agent sees only earned capabilities, and tool use changes shared story state. A general-purpose UI-driving agent could attempt the same flow, but with materially less reliable state, precision, and inspectability.
leverage_evidence: Frame sheets show a limited initial tool set and later 'Pencil found' / newly registered action states.
Frame sheets explicitly depict that the agent sees only what the story has earned.
The packet describes discoveries revealing new WebMCP actions and canonical state updates.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, intentional product concept with a complete authored mystery, manuscript UI, tool-state cards, and progressive document/story states. The frame sheets show a plausible staged workflow, but there is no transcript and no direct runtime demonstration of an end-to-end agent invocation, so completion credit is capped.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show consistent dark application/manuscript surfaces and progressive tool and document states.
Frame sheets show the discovery-to-tool-registration-to-updated-story loop conceptually.
Devpost packaging identifies a live demo link and a complete authored mystery, but the screenshot is packaging only.
impact_rationale: Interactive-fiction players and authors have a clear desire for free-form interaction without losing authored clues, causality, and mystery pacing. The proposed shared human-agent narrative model directly addresses that tension, with credible value for both play and experimentation even though audience scale is not established.
impact_evidence: The packet identifies interactive-fiction players as the intended audience and the tension between rigid choices and unconstrained generative stories.
The frame sheets visibly show a mystery manuscript, clue discovery, and evolving capabilities.
The product claims one complete authored mystery rather than only an abstract framework.
creativity_rationale: The project pursues a memorable interaction model in which narrative discoveries become agent capabilities, making the tool surface itself part of the fiction. Combining authored mystery causality, natural-language play, and progressively revealed WebMCP verbs is a notably original synthesis for a hackathon.
creativity_evidence: The packet frames each discovery as changing what AI can do, not merely changing prose.
Frame sheets show story-dependent action/tool inventory and a 'Pencil found' capability reveal.
The concept explicitly connects free-form play with authored causality and inspectable agent state.
usability_note: The manuscript and status-card presentation appears coherent and legible, but the packet does not establish access requirements or directly prove the live interaction path; the agent/tool workflow may require explanation for first-time users.
red_flags: Packet facts say video=False while frame sheets and the Devpost screenshot present demo-media evidence; the evidence surfaces are inconsistent.
No transcript or direct end-to-end runtime evidence is included, so agent invocation and live state mutation cannot be fully verified.
standouts: WebMCP capabilities are integrated into the fiction as earned narrative mechanics.
The human, agent, and authored page are intentionally framed as co-dependent participants.
Strong visual continuity between manuscript output and structured tool-state progression.
advance_reason: The project has a distinctive, high-potential WebMCP-native interaction model and enough coherent visual evidence to merit advancement, despite missing transcript/runtime proof and an inconsistency in the packet's video metadata.
